message.content: [罪名]故意毁坏财物罪;非法侵入住宅罪<eoa>
message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine crimes based on facts: Liu used a crowbar (撅头) and ladder to break into victim's house, smashed the security door, and destroyed property: two TVs, fridge, water dispenser, dining set, tea table, etc. Value 8817 yuan. This is property damage. In Chinese criminal law, damaging property intentionally is "故意毁坏财物罪". Also possibly "入室抢劫"? No theft, just damage. No theft of items, they were smashed. So crime: "故意毁坏财物罪". Also maybe "寻衅滋事罪"? But the fact is about property damage due to economic dispute. The main crime is intentional destruction of property. Could also be "非法侵入住宅罪"? Under Chinese law, illegal entry into a dwelling is "非法侵入住宅罪". However the facts: He used ladder to go to the house, broke door, entered? It says he smashed the door and smashed items inside. That implies illegal entry. The crime of illegal intrusion is separate. But the prosecution may charge "非法侵入住宅罪" (illegal intrusion into a private residence). However the fact mentions he used crowbar to smash the door and then smashed items. The primary crime is "故意毁坏财物罪". The illegal entry may be considered as "非法侵入住宅罪" if he entered. The facts: "使用撅头砸坏防盗门，又将屋内二台电视机...砸坏". It doesn't explicitly say he entered, but he smashed items inside, implying entry. So could be both.

But the instruction: "只写这部分事实直接支持的罪名". The facts support intentional property damage. Also support illegal intrusion. Chinese law: Article 245 of Criminal Law: "非法侵入住宅罪" - entering a private residence without permission. The fact: He used ladder to go to the house, smashed door, presumably entered. So yes.

Thus list: 故意毁坏财物罪;非法侵入住宅罪

Check if any other: "寻衅滋事罪" requires causing public disorder, not necessarily. So not.

Thus final answer format: [罪名]故意毁坏财物罪;非法侵入住宅罪<eoa>
